correctness.rationale: For 1<=a<=b and a<=3, N=a+b+1 and M=ab+a+b. Each vertex color class has s_c<N since the tripartite graph contains a triangle; the edge forest of color c avoids s_c vertices and has at most N-s_c-1 edges. Thus M<=k(N-1)-N; algebra gives k>=3 at a=1, >=4 at a=2, and >=4 for a=3,b<=5 or >=5 for b>=6. The explicit hub-color/part-color and AB-star coloring uses a+2 colors where needed. For the finite exceptional K_{1,3,5}, the RESULT.md vertex and 23 edge assignments avoid endpoint colors, give acyclic edge classes with edge counts 7,6,7,3 on the allowed 8,7,8,4 vertices and acyclic vertex-induced graphs; I checked all 23 edges, four forests, and capacity saturation independently. Deleting B columns preserves valid colorings for b=3,4. At (3,5), total forest capacity is exactly M=23, so every optimal coloring saturates each color capacity and gives a spanning tree. This establishes the entire a<=3 infinite family; finite checks only corroborate witness details.
residual_risks: Finite independent tests corroborate only tested parameters; universal argument is from source proof and standard theorem applications.
